subject: Networking lockstep: MAP & POC activation runbook
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Claire Park <cpark@medicore.com>, Medicore IT <netops@medicore.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Oct 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Networking lockstep: MAP & POC activation runbook

Hi Claire / Medicore network team —

Good to meet yesterday. As discussed, I wanted to centralize the mutual action plan (MAP) items we need to complete to bring a POC environment online for the evaluation: key things are org setup, API key issuance and rotation guidance, IP allowlist entries, and scheduling a VPC peering window for an initial connectivity test.

High-level ask: can you confirm which team will own the peering (NetOps or Cloud Infra) and what two-hour windows next week look like for the peering handshake?

Attached I’ve included a first-pass MAP (MAP_v1.pdf) and a simple network diagram to align on CIDR ranges. Proposed activation runbook (short):
- Day 0: Redwood creates pilot org + service account; share API key request form.
- Day 1: Medicore adds Redwood API egress IPs to allowlist.
- Day 2: VPC peering window & routing validation (2-hour window).
- Day 3: Smoke tests + sample inference runs; sign-off and handover to your SREs.

I’m looping Marissa (on enablement) and Ben (SE) to scope the test prompts and a short load profile for the smoke test.

Next step: Claire — can you confirm ownership & suggest two preferred peering windows next week? If you’d like, we can also add Hannah for any security questionnaire items.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive
Redwood Inference
From: Claire Park <cpark@medicore.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Medicore IT <netops@medicore.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Oct 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Networking lockstep: MAP & POC activation runbook

Jordan,

Thanks — that plan looks reasonable. A few clarifying points from our side:

1) Ownership: NetOps will own the peering setup, Cloud Infra will validate routing post-peering. I’ll coordinate internally and confirm the contact by end of day.
2) IP allowlist: we prefer to receive a consolidated list of the exact egress IPs and a short TTL window (we rotate lists on a 24h cadence). Can you include the source ports/protocols?
3) API key policy: Are you issuing one-time test keys for the POC, or do you need us to create a service account and request key material? We need rotation guidance to align with our compliance team.
4) Security artifacts: our audit team asked for SOC 2 Type II report and a short description of data handling during the POC.

For peering windows, our initial availability is: Mon 10/05 09:00–11:00 PDT or Tue 10/06 13:00–15:00 PDT. Either works.

Attaching our internal peering checklist (referenced) in-line as netops-checklist.docx (stub).

—Claire
Director, Cloud Architecture
Medicore
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Claire Park <cpark@medicore.com>, Medicore IT <netops@medicore.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2027 08:42:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Networking lockstep: MAP & POC activation runbook

Claire — great, thanks for the quick reply and the available windows. I’ve updated the MAP and attached a compact activation-action-items.csv that maps owners, target dates, and success criteria (attached: activation-action-items.csv).

Short answers to your bullets:
- IPs/protocols: we will provide a single egress range and port list (443 outbound) — see network-diagram.png. We’ll also include an alternate range in case you need a narrower allowlist.
- API keys: Redwood will provision a short-lived POC API key per your preferred model. Option A (our recommendation): Redwood issues a scoped API key tied to the pilot org that auto-expires after 14 days. Option B: Medicore creates a service account and issues the key; Redwood will provide the credentials format. Let us know preference.
- SOC2 & data handling: attached link to our SOC 2 summary + a brief POC data flow (we do not persist customer payloads beyond session in the POC unless explicitly requested).

Proposed mutual action timeline (we can compress if you want a faster runway):
- Tue 10/05 — NetOps peering window (09:00–11:00 PDT) 
  - Pre-check: CIDR confirm, VPC IDs, routing table edits documented.
  - During: establish peering, exchange route targets, test ICMP & HTTPS to the test endpoint.
- Wed 10/06 — Redwood config: pilot org plus scoped API key delivered; initial smoke runs.
- Thu 10/07 — Joint smoke & functional validation; iterate on prompts and token limits (Ben will lead).
- Fri 10/08 — Handover & acceptance sign-off or list of follow-ups.

If that timeline looks good, Jordan — would you mind sending an updated HubSpot timeline (I added the deal link to the MAP doc) and I’ll request DocuSign on the MAP so Medicore can sign the minimal POC agreement.

Thanks — looping Hannah for any additional security review items.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Customer Enablement Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Claire Park <cpark@medicore.com>, Peter Lang <peter.lang@medicore.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 06 Oct 2027 15:33:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Networking lockstep: MAP & POC activation runbook

Claire / Peter — thanks for confirming the windows. NetOps confirmed Tue 10/05 09:00–11:00 PDT works for the peering handshake. Peter — can you please share the peering contact and the jumpbox IP you’ll use for validation?

Two quick notes from security:
- SOC 2 summary and the POC data handling page are available at the Drive link Marissa shared; if you need the full report we can coordinate an NDA with our security team.
- On API keys: we recommend Option A (Redwood-issued scoped key that auto-expires). That reduces credential management for Medicore during the pilot. If you prefer Medicore-managed keys, we’ll send the service-account template.

Next steps:
1) Peter — share jumpbox IP + peering contact by EOD Monday.
2) NetOps & Redwood SE (Ben) to run pre-check checklist 1 hour before the peering window.
3) Marissa will circulate the DocuSign MAP link after we finalize the owner columns.

Looking forward — will be on standby during the Tue window for the validation.

Hannah Schmitt
Head of Onboarding (Redwood Inference)
